newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Three Gulf Arab states in Russian submarine talks.
newsitem.headline: Three Gulf Arab states in Russian submarine talks.

text.p: Three Gulf Arab states are in preliminary negotiations with Russia on the possibility of buying submarines from Moscow superior to those sold to Iran, a Russian official said on Wednesday.
"We are in the early stages of talks with three Gulf Arab states on submarines. We still don't know if they are interested in buying them," said the official, who requested anonymity.
He said the talks had been going on for six months but would not name the countries who are considering a purchase, citing confidentiality agreements.
"Right now, they are discussing the possibility of buying submarines. When a contract is signed we can give the specifics," he said on the sidelines of Abu Dhabi's international arms show IDEX.
Iran in January took delivery of its third Kilo diesel-powered submarine, giving Tehran additional military firepower and enhancing its ability to torpedo tankers carrying oil through the Gulf.
The Russian official said a sale of submarines would involve vessels that are an upgraded version of the type sold to Iran.
"The newer models are more powerful, those are the ones that are for export," he said.
Iran's Islamic republic, the only Gulf state to deploy submarines in the waterway, is seen by oil-rich Gulf Arab states as a threat to regional security.
The Russian official declined to say why the three Gulf Arab states were holding initial talks on submarines.
"I don't know their purposes," he said.

Non-Arab Iran launched a programme to upgrade its weaponry after its military was bled by the 1980-88 war with Iraq. Its arms buildup has focused on its navy in the strategic Gulf which sits on about 70 percent of the world's oil reserves.
When asked if Iran had shown an interest in any more submarine purchases or if talks were underway, the Russian official said: "At the moment no."
He said it would take the Iranians about a year to learn how to operate their new Russian-made submarine.
Russia has boosted and polished its presence at this year's IDEX, one of the world's biggest arms shows.
A senior Russian defence industry official on Tuesday said Moscow was seeking to grab 40 percent of the Gulf arms market by 1999.
